questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/33f7326ffe8318fca915e8cc7e02a2a4c280dd9377066f1870f3bb8067b22eb0.png)

Consider the segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ above, and the transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=2u+3v+2,\,y=v-2u.
$$

The image of $\overset{―}{PQ}$ under the action of $T$ is the segment $\overset{―}{{P}^{′}{Q}^{′}}$ in the $xy$-plane. Which of the following diagrams shows $\overset{―}{{P}^{′}{Q}^{′}}?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u+3v+2 \\ v-2u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\,2u+3v \\ -2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the endpoints of $\overset{―}{PQ}$ to the endpoints of $\overset{―}{{P}^{′}{Q}^{′}}.$ So, to find the image of $\overset{―}{PQ},$ we find the images of each endpoint.

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing the endpoints of our segment:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & 8 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 10 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the endpoints of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(-5,3)$ and $(10,0).$

Drawing this segment in the $xy$-plane, we get the following: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/e4bea3edd3fcde575e68e36e08fc4186863b12450802eb0ee37c841975983486.png)

questions.problem:
Consider the transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=3v+u,\,y=u-6v+3.
$$

Let $P(-2,3)$ be a point in the $uv$-plane. Suppose that the image of $P$ under the action of $T$ is the point ${P}^{′}$ in the $xy$-plane. What are the coordinates of ${P}^{′}?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3v+u \\ u-6v+3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+3v \\ u-6v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the image of $P$ under the action of $T,$ we first create a column vector $u$ containing the coordinates of $P:$

$$
u=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Applying $T$ to $u,$ we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -17\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of ${P}^{′}$ are $(7,-17).$

questions.problem:
Consider the transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=-v+u+2,\,y=u+v-1.
$$

Let $P(4,1)$ be a point in the $uv$-plane. Suppose that the image of $P$ under the action of $T$ is the point ${P}^{′}$ in the $xy$-plane. What are the coordinates of ${P}^{′}?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-v+u+2 \\ u+v-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the image of $P$ under the action of $T,$ we first create a column vector $u$ containing the coordinates of $P:$

$$
u=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Applying $T$ to $u,$ we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of ${P}^{′}$ are $(5,4).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Polygon Under an Affine Transformation
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/79b09bcf02998adf6d7bf19e7d59cabdc563ff26266966440bbb49be53029ac3.png)

Consider the triangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,-\frac{u+1}{2}\le v\le u+1}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation is already in matrix form 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/539c74bf4d397916fd7ac11089fa9500bd71cdf2278891136785d6e792431b05.png)

             

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our triangle:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(-1,-1),(1,-1),$ and $(-2,2).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/adfe476bd2ca719996d612855ca5368bdea09370b7befcffb08a062db8587cbb.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=-1<0,$ this transformation is not orientation-preserving.

Consider the triangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1-u}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation is already in matrix form 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/0d736c2e3fa2c4ba1872b045b8bdcf4def98a24337683e368bec337b810b6acb.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our triangle:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(0,-1),(1,0),$ and $(-2,0).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/1aed421f9d6458fb8b72a44c83703b3f1c0475cee9ef9ec2f0a4cfcaad74d7fc.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=3>0,$ this transformation preserves orientation.

questions.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=2v+u+1,\,y=u-v-2.
$$

Let $A$ be the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]$
- $det(A)=-3$
- The transformation $T$ is orientation-preserving
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Let's look at each statement in turn:

- Statement I is false. Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2v+u+1 \\ u-v-2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+2v \\ u-v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].$

- Statement II is true. Indeed, computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|=1\cdot (-1)-2\cdot 1=-3.
$$

- Statement III is false. Since $det(A)<0,$ the affine transformation $T$ is not orientation-preserving.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

questions.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
x=v-u,\,y=u+v-1.
$$

What is the area scale factor of the transformation?
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}v-u \\ u+v-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-u+v \\ u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|=1\cdot (-1)-1\cdot 1=-2.
$$

So, the area scale factor of the transformation is

$$
|det(A)|=|-2|=2.
$$

Consider the segment $\overline{PQ}$ above, and the transformation $\mathbf T$ defined as

$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v+7 \\ u+v+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $\mathbf T$ maps the endpoints of $\overline{PQ}$ to the endpoints of $\overline{P'Q'}.$ So, to find the image of $\overline{PQ},$ we find the images of each endpoint.

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing the endpoints of our segment:

$$
[\begin{aligned}-5 & -5 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $\mathbf b$ in each column:

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & 7 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $\mathbf u$ under $\mathbf T$ is given by $A\mathbf u + \mathbf b.$ So, by applying $\mathbf T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 & -5 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}7 & 7 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & -10 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}7 & 7 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the endpoints of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(0,-2)$ and $(-3,1).$

- Statement I is true. Indeed, notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}v-u-6 \\ v-2u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-u+v \\ -2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $\mathbf T$ is $[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]$

- Statement II is true. Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is true. Indeed, since $\det(A) > 0,$ the affine transformation $\mathbf T$ is orientation-preserving.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Area Scale Factor of an Affine Transformation
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $\mathbf T,$ defined as

$$
x = 3u+4, \qquad y = 4v - 2u.
$$

What is the area scale factor of the transformation?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3u+4 \\ 4v-2u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u \\ -2u+4v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $\mathbf T$ is $[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the area scale factor of the transformation is

$$
|\det(A)| = |12| =12.
$$
